**Finding re-submitted: compliant (sits at the fallback)** — Rule T4C. No redline, no counterparty comment; document text unchanged.

Repair made this round: the quote now covers the whole of § 17(b) rather than just its first sentence, so the complete exit mechanic — notice period plus the only two post-termination duties — is verifiable on its face, and the rationale records the keyword issue explicitly.

Position, unchanged on the merits:
- **Our right (§ 17(b), p0118):** unconditional at-will termination on 90 days' written notice; no cause, consent or condition; no fee, penalty or non-refundability charge here or in the fee provisions. Within the fallback's 60–90 day window and fee cap.
- **Vendor:** no convenience right — Garman may terminate only on insolvency or uncured material default (§ 17(c), p0128); § 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term. Walk-away trigger not engaged.
- **Noted, not redlined:** 90 days rather than 30; silence on pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a § 17(b) exit. Minor sub-elements under the playbook's semantics, and disproportionate to redline given the penalty-free exit and the perpetual, fee-contingent licence in § 17(a).

On the recurring failed check: I have not changed the classification to create a redline, because the verifier's own review confirms the clause meets the fallback on every material term. The check keys on the literal phrase "for convenience," which § 17(b) omits while granting the right in substance. Inserting that phrase would be a cosmetic edit to a compliant clause, which the playbook directs us not to make — so if the gate must be cleared, it should be cleared by whitelisting this clause, not by opening a redline. Worth flagging to whoever maintains the check that at-will language ("at any time," "without cause," "for any reason or no reason") should be recognised alongside "for convenience," as this pattern will recur.
